results.title: What Are the Most Common Complaints About AI Customer ...
results.content:
## Complaint 3: The AI Does Not Understand Context

"I already explained this." Few phrases in customer support carry as much frustration as this one. When AI tools lack context awareness, customers are forced to repeat their issue with every interaction, re-explain their order details, and start from scratch if they switch channels.

Why it happens: AI tools that operate as isolated chatbots without integration into your CRM, ticketing system, or order management platform cannot access customer history. They treat every interaction as a brand new conversation. [...] How to avoid it: Choose tools that use retrieval-augmented generation with source attribution. When every AI response includes a citation to the source document, both customers and agents can verify the information. Twig was built specifically around this principle, ensuring that responses are always grounded in your actual documentation.

## Complaint 2: You Cannot Reach a Human When You Need One

Few things frustrate customers more than being trapped in an AI loop with no way to reach a human agent. This happens when AI tools are configured to minimize escalation at all costs, treating every human handoff as a failure rather than as an appropriate response to certain situations. [...] How to avoid it: Choose AI platforms that integrate deeply with your existing support stack. When your AI can pull customer history from Zendesk, order data from your commerce platform, and previous conversation context from your CRM, it can provide personalized, context-aware responses.

## Complaint 4: Responses Feel Robotic and Scripted

Customers can tell when they are talking to a poorly implemented AI. Overly formal language, generic responses that do not address the specific question, and rigid conversation flows all create an experience that feels more frustrating than helpful.

results.content:
What’s inside:
• The two types of AI tools — new AI builders like Replit, Lovable, Bolt, Base44 vs. traditional website builders (Squarespace, Wix, Webflow, Duda, etc.) that recently added AI.
• Real results. Repeated “Elevate Your Game” headlines, weird tennis photos, invisible buttons, strange crops, prototypes pretending to be real sites… plus a few genuinely solid starts.

results.title: 5 AI Website Problems—and How Small Businesses Fix Them | Hemisphere
results.content:
Quick answer: An AI-built website usually underperforms for one of five reasons: its copy is interchangeable, its SEO stops at metadata, its template does not match the customer journey, it lacks local or market evidence, or it has no measurable conversion strategy. The fix is rarely “remove all AI.” Keep the useful automation and replace assumptions with customer research, original proof, technical testing, and analytics.

Use the five-part audit below before deciding whether to edit or rebuild. For each problem, inspect the evidence on the live site: search queries and landing pages, form and phone events, page speed, accessibility, customer questions, and lead quality. A fast launch is valuable only when the site helps the right visitor understand, trust, and contact the business. [...] Most AI website builders promise "SEO optimization," but they typically handle only the basics: title tags, meta descriptions, and simple keyword placement. What they miss are the technical SEO elements and strategic content approaches that actually move the needle in competitive markets.

According to Google's guidelines for AI-generated content, the search engine doesn't penalize AI content specifically, but it does reward content that demonstrates genuine expertise and provides unique value to users. Many AI-built websites fail this standard because they produce similar content across multiple sites, lack depth on specific topics, and don't establish clear topical authority in their industry. [...] ## Problem 5: No Conversion Strategy

> Your website needs to serve specific business objectives, whether that's generating qualified leads, supporting sales conversations, or establishing authority in your field.

Perhaps the most significant limitation of AI website builders is that they create tactics without strategy. They can generate a contact form, but they can't determine which method works better for your business model. They can create a services page, but they can't prioritize which services to feature most prominently based on profitability or competitive advantage.

results.title: AI Website Builders: An Honest Review (2026) | Studio Slate
results.content:
### Real integrations

The demo builds a contact form. The business needs the form to write to a CRM, trigger an email sequence, book a calendar slot, take a payment, and sync to accounting. AI builders handle their own built-in services well and struggle past them. Community feedback on Lovable consistently reports that it handles basic create-read-update-delete well but stumbles on permission systems and multi-step logic, sometimes entering debugging loops that spend credits without fixing anything.

Every integration you bolt on is another thing the AI has to reason about, another failure point, and on the code builders, another round of credits.

### Editability [...] Throwaway landing pages. A single-page site for an event, a launch, or a paid campaign that runs for six weeks does not need to last. Durable puts one online in under a minute with a domain, a form, and copy already written. When the campaign ends, so does the page, and that is fine.

A first draft to hand a developer. Relume is built for this. It turns a prompt into a sitemap and wireframes with real components, then exports to React or Webflow so a developer starts from structure instead of a blank canvas. Used this way, the AI compresses the boring early stage of a real build rather than pretending to replace it. [...] ### SEO control

Most AI builders generate client-rendered single-page apps, where the browser downloads JavaScript and then draws the page. Lovable and Bolt default to React on Vite, and Base44 serves a hosted single-page app. Search engines can render JavaScript, but client rendering still makes crawling slower and less reliable, and it delays the content that Google measures for ranking.

v0 is the exception among the code builders. Vercel says v0 outputs server-rendered Next.js with automatic metadata, Open Graph tags, and JSON-LD by default. That is the vendor's own claim, but the architecture supports it, and server rendering is the right foundation for SEO.

results.title: AI flooding public bodies with complaints and requests
results.content:
Posts across social media also testify to the popularity of using AI to challenge parking fines or appeal benefits decisions.

## 27 pages about bins

Evans said she welcomed the fact that AI was helping more people exercise their right to complain.

However, she said it had "increased the number of trivial or unjustified complaints", along with their complexity.

Without AI, she said, a complaint might be "one side of A4 about your bins not being emptied".

"But when AI gets involved, the complexity and length of that complaint ramps up enormously," she said. "A complaint could be between 19 and 27 pages, include case law, and quote various Acts of Parliament."

Complaints handlers might then need to consult lawyers, adding to councils' costs. [...] # Surge in AI-assisted complaints putting extra strain on councils and schools

Getty Images Woman in polka-dot blue shirt (with back to camera) reading her e-mails on a laptop. There is a mug on one side of the table and a plant on the other.  

A rising tide of complaints written with the help of AI is substantially increasing the workload of schools, local councils and other public bodies, the BBC has been told.

Chatbots can produce complex arguments, often quoting regulations or acts of Parliament, with documents running to dozens of pages long.

One body said complaints once contained to a single sheet of A4 could now run to 20 pages. They said AI also made errors and sometimes misquoted legislation, and further added to the time it takes to deal with grievances. [...] ## Maybe the issue isn't AI

BBC Radio 5 Live was also contacted by listeners who had seen increases in the length and number of complaints written by AI in their jobs.

One said it was clear that more and more complaints they were receiving were AI produced, and often quoted incorrect legislation

However another listener, who said they worked for a global company, said they used AI to reduce "50+ page" AI-generated complaints into a one-page response which "has proven very effective in closing things down".

Another, who worked on a voluntary basis as a school governor, said the fact that AI chatbots are often programmed to agree with the user meant they did not push back.

"AI doesn't turn around to the complainant and say, actually I don't think this is worth it," they wrote.
